advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the survivor-budget vs unknown-survivor logic: either record the equivalent fingerprints for signing/next-batch or make `unknown-survivor` only fire once `survivors_max` is exhausted, so a non-zero survivors_max is actually reachable.
evidence: scripts/mutation_gate.py:279 `if counts["survived"] > shard.survivors_max:` then :281-286 loops all survived mutants and yields `unknown-survivor` when `head.fingerprints.get(mutant) not in shard.equivalent_fingerprints`
.github/mutation-shards.toml:20-24 `survivors_max = 3` with `equivalent_fingerprints = []` for signing; :45-49 `survivors_max = 6` with `equivalent_fingerprints = []` for next-batch

Old docs/mutation-testing.md recorded signing.py has 3 equivalent survivors and next_batch.py has 6 — with no recorded fingerprints, each survivor triggers `unknown-survivor` and the shard fails despite the budget
advisory.finding: For shards with a non-zero `survivors_max` but empty `equivalent_fingerprints` (e.g. `signing` survivors_max=3, `next-batch` survivors_max=6), the `unknown-survivor` check hard-fails on EVERY survived mutant regardless of the survivor budget, making the non-zero budget dead configuration and forcing those shards to block on their known-equivalent survivors.
scenarios: A run of the `signing` or `next-batch` shard that reproduces its documented equivalent survivors

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Run each selected shard as its own matrix job with an independent 30-minute cap (or otherwise bound total runtime) rather than iterating all shards in one 30-minute job.
evidence: .github/workflows/_mutation.yml:30-34 single `mutation` job, `timeout-minutes: 30`, no `strategy.matrix`
.github/workflows/_mutation.yml:62-64 `--all-shards` runs every shard in that one job
scripts/mutation_gate.py:395-402 unconditionally `_extract_ref(repo, args.base ...)` + `execute_shard(base_root ...)` then head for every shard (base always run, no mode gating)

Ticket AC: 'Workflows use selector-derived per-shard matrix jobs with a 30-minute limit each'; ticket comment: 'A single 30-minute base+head all-shard job is also not credibly bounded' and signing alone left mutants unchecked after ~10 minutes at --max-children 1
advisory.finding: `_mutation.yml` runs all selected shards (and the weekly `--all-shards` sweep) in a single job under one `timeout-minutes: 30` cap, and the driver always executes both base and head archives per shard, rather than the per-shard matrix jobs (30-minute cap each) the ticket AC requires; the ticket's own probe evidence indicates a single all-shard 30-minute job is not credibly bounded.
scenarios: A patchset touching global_support that selects every shard

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the modeless single-policy gate is the intended walking-skeleton scope, or add the advisory/ratchet/strict enforcement the ticket ACs specify.
evidence: search for `mode` and `advisory` in scripts/mutation_gate.py returned `(no matches)`
.github/mutation-shards.toml:15-24 shard tables have no `mode` key
Ticket ACs reference advisory/ratchet/strict behavior extensively (e.g. 'Advisory returns success for survived... findings', 'Manifest loading accepts only advisory, ratchet, or strict')
advisory.finding: The implemented gate has no `advisory`/`ratchet`/`strict` per-shard enforcement mode, yet the ticket plan and multiple acceptance criteria are entirely defined in terms of those modes (advisory head-only, ratchet base/head, strict full-shard); the manifest carries no `mode` field and the driver never branches on one.
scenarios: Any reviewer expecting the ticket-described advisory-first rollout

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm uv.lock includes mutmut==3.7.0 plus all new transitive deps (with hashes) and is consistent with pyproject.toml under `--locked`.
evidence: pyproject.toml adds `"mutmut==3.7.0"` to the dev extra
_mutation.yml runs `uv sync --locked --extra dev` which fails if pyproject and uv.lock disagree
uv.lock is listed among the changed files but its diff body is truncated/not shown for verification
advisory.finding: Verify that uv.lock was regenerated to include mutmut==3.7.0 and its full transitive closure with hashes, so `uv sync --locked --extra dev` in the CI workflows does not fail on an out-of-date lockfile.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for function_hashes()/_module_name(): identical AST -> same hash, semantic edit -> different hash, method-in-class naming, and src.-prefix/__init__ stripping.
evidence: scripts/mutation_gate.py defines `def function_hashes(root: Path, source: str) -> dict[str, str]` and `def _module_name(source: str)` which build the `unit_hashes` keys used by evaluate_runs

tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py `_run(...)` helper takes `hashes=hashes or {}` — every comparison test supplies hashes literally; search for `function_hashes` in the test file returns (no matches)

ABSENCE: no test parses a real source unit and asserts its hash stays equal across a whitespace/rename-only edit and changes across a semantic edit — the exact refactor-vs-edit distinction the gate's correctness rests on
advisory.finding: function_hashes() and _module_name() — the AST-based per-unit hash that decides whether a mutation unit is 'unchanged' (and therefore whether a killed->survived transition gates) — have no direct test. All comparison tests (test_unchanged_unit_*, test_renamed_units_*) inject unit_hashes as hand-written dict literals, so the actual hashing/naming that classifies a real edit vs. a behavior-preserving refactor is never exercised.
advisory.suggested_fix: Write a source snippet to a tmp file, call function_hashes(tmp, 'src/x.py'), assert the qualified keys and that an unrelated-whitespace edit preserves the digest while a `>=`->`>` edit changes it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where a same-named unit has a DIFFERENT hash base vs head and a killed->survived transition: assert no killed-regression/missing-mutant failure is raised (only head budgets apply).
evidence: scripts/mutation_gate.py evaluate_runs: `for mutant, status in base.statuses.items(): if status != 'killed' or unit_name(mutant) not in unchanged_units: continue` — the same-name-but-changed-hash path is the `not in unchanged_units` branch

tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py test_unchanged_unit_blocks_killed_to_non_killed_transition uses hashes={'pkg.x_f':'same'} on both sides; test_renamed_units_* changes the unit NAME (x_foo->x_bar), not the hash of a same-named unit
docs/mutation-testing.md: 'Mutant IDs can move after a legitimate edit, so these units use the head shard budgets instead of an exact-ID comparison.'
advisory.finding: evaluate_runs() is only tested for the UNCHANGED-unit killed->non-killed gate and the fully-renamed-unit case; there is no test that a CHANGED unit keeping the same qualified name (differing hash) does NOT raise killed-regression. The 'edited units use head budgets instead of exact-ID comparison' contract (docs/mutation-testing.md) is therefore unverified — a regression here would let the gate either over-flag legitimate edits or (if inverted) miss real regressions.
advisory.suggested_fix: base = _run(gate, {'pkg.x_f__mutmut_1':'killed'}, hashes={'pkg.x_f':'old'}); head = _run(gate, {'pkg.x_f__mutmut_1':'survived'}, hashes={'pkg.x_f':'new'}, fingerprints=...); assert 'killed-regression' not in {f.code for f in compare_runs(shard, base, head)}.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for _diagnose_non_killed: with all-killed statuses returns 'stable'; monkeypatch the mutmut rerun so a survived mutant flips -> assert 'nondeterminism'; unchanged -> 'stable'.
evidence: scripts/mutation_gate.py `_diagnose_non_killed` reruns mutmut and returns 'nondeterminism' if `after.get(name) != head.statuses[name]` else 'stable'
docs/mutation-testing.md: 'When head has a non-killed result, the driver reruns it once for diagnosis; a changed outcome is labeled nondeterministic, but the gate remains red.'

ABSENCE: no test in tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py references _diagnose_non_killed or asserts the stable/nondeterminism labeling (the parse_results + rerun comparison is pure enough to test with a stubbed _run)
advisory.finding: _diagnose_non_killed() — the documented 'rerun a non-killed head result once, label it nondeterminism if the outcome changes but keep the gate red' flakiness contract — has no test. This is a behavior the change explicitly introduces (docs 'Flakiness and false positives') and a regression that turned a red gate green on rerun, or mislabeled stable as nondeterministic, would go undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch gate._run to return canned mutmut `results` stdout and assert the returned label for a changed vs unchanged rerun.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for _without_mutmut_table: input with a [tool.mutmut] table between two other tables returns text with that table removed and both neighbors intact.
evidence: scripts/mutation_gate.py `_without_mutmut_table` toggles `skipping` on `[tool.mutmut]` until the next `[` header

tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py test_mutmut_config_is_generated_from_one_shard only tests render_mutmut_config, not the strip-and-splice in _prepare_config/_without_mutmut_table; search for `_without_mutmut_table` in tests returns (no matches)
advisory.finding: _without_mutmut_table() — which strips the (now-removed) [tool.mutmut] table from pyproject before appending the per-shard generated config — has no test, yet its correctness is load-bearing: a bug leaving a stale table or eating the following section would silently mis-configure every mutation run.
advisory.suggested_fix:
assert _without_mutmut_table('[a]
x=1
[tool.mutmut]
y=2
[b]
z=3
') drops only the mutmut block and keeps [a] and [b].

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify HEAD^ resolves to the patchset's real parent on both the Gerrit patchset checkout and the push/PR merge-commit checkout (fetch-depth:2), or derive the base explicitly.
evidence: .github/workflows/_mutation.yml:40 `fetch-depth: 2` and :61/:64 `--base HEAD^ --head HEAD`
scripts/mutation_gate.py:always uses args.base default 'HEAD^' (see _parser child.add_argument('--base', default='HEAD^'))
ABSENCE: no handling for a PR merge-commit head where HEAD^ is the base-branch tip rather than the change's parent
dropped.finding: The driver diffs `HEAD^..HEAD` from the checked-out ref, but the branch/PR checkout uses `fetch-depth: 2` and GitHub PR events check out a synthetic merge commit whose first parent is the base branch tip; `HEAD^..HEAD` on that merge commit does not correspond to the patchset's own parent, so shard selection can be computed against the wrong base on the push/PR mirror lane.
scenarios: A pull_request-triggered run of test.yml's mutation job on a multi-commit branch

ABSENCE: no note about mutmut's transitive dependency set or its license implications
dropped.finding: mutmut==3.7.0 is newly added as a dev dependency but its transitive dependencies' license posture is not documented in the change; a new tool pulls in a dependency subtree whose licenses have not been reviewed here.
